attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice rather than quoted from someone else.

semantics.note: The checkable assertion is that FSD was improving. The drafter correctly treats the follow-up as an ungraded question and does not turn it into doubt or a negative forecast.

contract.note: Marcus named no period or metric. Reading this as recent improvement before the 2024-04-09 post (the v12 rollout), shown by disengagement data or reported driving quality, is an ordinary plain reading that is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: Dated 2024-04-02, before the post. Community tracker data shows v12.3 at roughly 3x the best v11 figure for miles between critical disengagements. It comes from an enthusiast blog with self-reported, small-sample data, and the article itself says v12.3 data was still coming in.

Dated 2024-03-18. Reports broad owner feedback that v12.3 drives more smoothly and makes decisions it could not make before. Comes from an enthusiast outlet; the Tesla director's remarks it cites are company statements, not independent findings.

reviews.rationale: Two items dated before the post show v12.3 doing better than earlier versions: one on disengagement rates, one on reported driving behavior. Both sources are enthusiast outlets and the tracker sample is small, but the packet contains no counterevidence. On the contract's plain reading, the claim that FSD was getting better holds. The 'enough better' question is not graded.
